title: ParticipantSelfDescription
description: The SOURCE self-description a participant keeps in its OWN repository (decisions/ADR-0007-self-describing-participant.md decision 7): one reviewable document stating where its four facets — identity, capability, egress, translation — live, so what it serves can be derived from and checked against a declared intent instead of hand-maintained. It is NOT a second manifest and is NOT served: the runtime self-description is the KCB AgentCard extension (specs/capability-bus.md §2), which this document only points at and which stays authoritative. Bounded by ADR-0007 decision 7 to pointers and references, never payloads — it references the KCB manifest shape rather than restating it, and embeds no bridge/predicate mapping entries, no topology, and no node/edge ontology (those are the deployment's instance data and stay in the participant's own repo, per CLAUDE.md). Koine holds this shape only; the filled-in values never come here. Role-scoped: the illustrative values in the field descriptions and in the golden positive at schemas/fixtures/participant-self-description.json use the KINP identity.md §3.4 placeholder namespaces (refkb / worldsim / analyzer / mediastore / orchestrator / provider). Validators live downstream per ADR-0001, NOT in koine.

kinpId.description: A KINP CURIE — namespace:kind:local (identity.md §3.2), e.g. orchestrator:agent:composer, provider:agent:transcoder.

namespacePrefix.description: A KINP namespace prefix (identity.md §3.4) — the minting authority's name. Reserved to exactly one authority and immutable once published.

location.description: A pointer to where an artifact lives — a path inside the participant's own repository, and/or the URL it is served at. A pointer only: this document never carries the artifact itself. At least one of path / url is required.

path.description: Path relative to the root of the participant's OWN repository. Never a path into another participant's repo — no participant reads another's repository (ADR-0007 decision 4).

url.description: Absolute URL the artifact is served at, where it is served at all. Serving any facet beyond the capability facet is OPTIONAL (ADR-0007, alternatives considered).

note.description: Free-text note for a human reader of this document.

self_description_version.description: The version of this document's shape (semver), declared per artifact.

participant.description: The KINP id of the participant this document describes — the same id its A2A AgentCard carries as its own agent id (KCB §2).

roles.description: The roles this participant claims. Role-scoped, never product-scoped: a participant publishes the facets the roles it claims reach (ADR-0007 decision 1).

identity.description: The identity facet (KINP identity.md §3.2–§3.4, §4.4, §6): the namespace this participant mints under, and the fact that it is the sole minting authority for it.

namespace.description: The prefix this participant mints under, as registered by PR in KINP §3.4. Registration reserves a name, not config — what is minted under it stays entirely with the participant.

minting_authority.description: Whether this participant is the sole minting authority for the namespace above (KINP §3.4). A participant that only reads ids minted elsewhere sets this false.

kinds.description: The KINP kinds minted under the namespace (identity.md §2, §3.2) — e.g. entity, asset, activity, world, agent, model.

external_anchors.description: External authority namespaces this participant anchors to (KINP §4.4) — e.g. wikidata, musicbrainz, geonames. Never minted by a Koine participant.

minting_rules.description: Pointer to where the participant records its own local-id scheme and reconciliation practice (KINP §6, offline-first). The rules themselves stay in the participant's repo.

capability.description: The capability facet (KCB capability-bus.md §2, §2.1) — BY REFERENCE ONLY. The manifest payload (kcb_version, produces / consumes ports, capabilities with cost, auth, signing) is defined by KCB §2 and served in the AgentCard extension's params; it is deliberately NOT restated here, and additionalProperties:false keeps it from creeping in. What this block carries is where the served card is, which extension identifies the manifest on it, and where the in-repo source that card is generated from lives.

agent_card.description: Where the participant serves its A2A AgentCard — conventionally its own /.well-known/agent-card.json. This is the authoritative, runtime self-description; no copy held elsewhere is authoritative (ADR-0007 decision 2).

manifest_extension_uri.description: The stable KCB extension URI identifying the manifest entry in the card's capabilities.extensions[] — currently https://w3id.org/koine/kcb/manifest/0.3, a w3id.org permanent identifier (KCB §2). This field is what the participant declares it SERVES, so it takes the form a conformant producer MUST emit; a consumer's obligation to also match the superseded root during the transition window is KCB §2's clause, not this schema's (no schema here models the AgentCard extension entry itself). There is no second well-known file: a 0.2.0-style standalone /.well-known/kcb-manifest.json is superseded (KCB §2.2).

manifest_source.description: Pointer to the reviewed in-repo source the served extension params are generated from, where the participant keeps one. A pointer, not the manifest: the payload's shape is KCB §2's, and the served card remains authoritative.

mcp.description: The participant's MCP tools endpoint, where it serves one — the non-A2A endpoint the extension still names as a plain params field (KCB §2).

egress.description: The egress facet (KGP grounding-pack.md §7.1, §7.2) — by reference: which relations and records are exportable and which are local-only, and the license classes released under, are the participant's own policy values and live in its own repo.

policy.description: Pointer to the participant's egress policy — the per-relation / per-record exportable vs local-only assignment (KGP §7.2). Never inlined here.

default_class.description: The egress class this participant applies to a record whose policy is unstated. exportable is KGP's default; a participant holding sensitive data may default to local-only.

license_policy.description: Pointer to the license classes this participant releases under and the allowlist it admits on (KGP §7.1, policy/license-classes.json).

enforced_at.description: Where enforcement happens, and the only conformant answer: in the emitting producer at pack construction, before any encoding is emitted (KGP §7.2, ADR-0007 decision 5). No central component ever holds a participant's egress rules.

translation.description: The translation facet (KGP §5, §7; registry/README.md) — LOCATIONS ONLY. Bridge / predicate mapping entries are a deployment's instance data and MUST NOT be committed into koine or embedded here; this block records where they live in the participant's own repo. A participant on the knowledge plane declares this even as a pure consumer, because it MUST reject a pack carrying local-only content (KGP §7.2) and can only do so against a stated policy.

mappings.description: One entry per mapping document the participant maintains — a pointer plus which direction of data it governs. The mapping rows themselves stay in the participant's repo.

direction.description: Whether this mapping governs data the participant emits, data it accepts, or both (ADR-0007 decision 1).

location.description: Where the mapping document lives in the participant's own repo.

plane.description: The plane whose vocabulary this mapping crosses into, using KCB §2.1's port planes.

note.description: Free-text note for a human reader.

target_registries.description: The shared koine relation files a mapping normalizes into — e.g. registry/relations.tsv, registry/relations/media.tsv. A mapping coins no relation name: closing a gap means adding a row to one of these, never naming a relation only in a mapping (registry/README.md).

discovery.description: How this participant is indexed, if it is. The discovery registry (KCB §3) returns an ADDRESS to a self-description, never the self-description (ADR-0007 decision 3): a registry entry is a cache and an index, never a source of truth.

registries.description: Registries the participant advertises its card address to. Optional in every sense — the participant MUST remain fully functional, and fully describable to a peer that dials it directly, with every registry unavailable.

registry_optional.description: Restates the invariant: discoverable without being dependent (ADR-0007 decision 3). The only conformant value is true.
